study_identification_part.si_4_title: Normative modelling of brain function abnormalities in complex pathology needs the whole brain

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: The study introduces FUNCOIN (Functional Connectivity Integrative Normative Modelling) as a novel whole-brain approach to normative modelling of FC. FUNCOIN is an adaptation of covariate-assisted principal regression, which performs simultaneous dimensionality reduction and regression of covariance matrices using a log-linear model.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: To fill this gap, we introduce Functional Connectivity Integrative Normative Modelling (FUNCOIN) as a method to evaluate how pathology pushes individuals from the normative range of brain function at a system level. FUNCOIN is an adaptation of a recently developed method from statistics literature, covariate-assisted principal regression, which performs simultaneous dimensionality reduction and regression of covariance matrices.

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: The study uses functional connectivity (FC) calculated as the Pearson correlation matrix from all pairs of 55 ICA components derived from resting-state fMRI data.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: Our measure of brain function is FC, determined in this case as the Pearson correlation matrix from all pairs of the parcellation components
nm2_2_response_variable.location: Kobbersmed2025.pdf.md: Results / Whole-brain normative modelling of FC

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: The FUNCOIN model used sex, age, and sex-age interaction as covariates. Age was linearly transformed to the interval [0,1]. Sex was coded as a categorical variable (0=female, 1=male).
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: We included sex, age, and sex-age interaction as covariates. The age variable was linearly transformed the interval [0,1], with 0 and 1 corresponding to the minimum and maximum age in the whole dataset (44.56 and 85.43 years). Sex was coded as a categorical variable with 0 denoting female, 1 denoting male.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.location: Kobbersmed2025.pdf.md: Materials and methods / Model fitting
